originalPrompts:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a polished landscape game-map concept board for the first introductory level of "Tower", a friendly software-development tower defense game. This is a proposed map design, not a screenshot of an implemented level.
Style: beautiful chunky low-poly 3D diorama, deliberate beveled forms, matte palette surfaces, soft daylight, gentle ambient shadows, warm welcoming technology campus integrated with nature. Fixed high orthographic isometric camera, whole route and objective visible. Strong clean silhouettes at mobile scale. Slate blue paths #48647D, small cyan path signals #82DADD, chalk architecture #E2EDF0, architectural blue-gray #89A4B8, soft teal foliage #70B5B4 plus theme-appropriate natural colors. No cyberpunk, no military guns, no photorealism.
Board design: refined off-white background, large clear title at top; about 78% of board devoted to one generous isometric map render; right-side compact tactical TOP-DOWN diagram of the SAME route. The diagram should be mechanically clear, less decorative, with one thick continuous dark route line, several small forward arrowheads, entrance circle, Product square, solid rectangular Server footprint, and six lightly outlined candidate deployment regions beside the route. These regions illustrate free placement choices, NOT mandatory tower pads. Do not place towers on the route or on the Server. Show two small friendly tech robot tower placeholders beside the route only, with no weapons. Two warm small moving task-card objects with check/progress symbols and one small blue jagged bug problem share the same route and move in the same direction. They are readable scale cues, not crowds. One Server building provides the only deliberate line-of-sight obstacle. The Product destination is a larger calmer friendly application-building with a big simple code symbol and clear arrival forecourt. No additional roads, disconnected path snippets, alternate routes, branching, crossings, closed loops, or teleporters. Low scenery must not cover moving entities. One spawn/start and one end.
Minimal diagram labels exactly: "ENTRY", "SERVER", "PRODUCT". A compact legend exactly: "Route" / "Placement areas" / "Sight blocker". Footer exactly: "Concept study - layout and balance to validate". Render a generous, attractive world and a clean useful diagram. No detailed stats or extra UI.
Title exactly: "01  HELLO WORLD COURTYARD"
Subtitle exactly: "A small feature, a clear first decision"
Scene/theme: intimate landscaped technology-campus courtyard, mint lawn, two clusters of round low-poly trees at rear margins, tiny ornamental pond in an unused corner, bench and planter, compact cable conduits and welcome signage. Infrastructure integrated with landscape. Product is a modest chalk-and-teal studio with a rounded application display and room for one later growth module.
Route topology: one gentle open S curve. In a top-down rectangular plan, ENTRY is at upper-left (8%,23%). Travel rightward through (30%,23%), curve around a CENTRAL small rectangular SERVER at (48%,44%), pass down through (49%,65%), curve back right through (70%,65%), end at PRODUCT lower-right (90%,65%). The actual paved route must follow that unbranched S shape in both views, remaining clearly separate from the Server footprint. No giant double hairpin. The Server stands just beside the middle bend with open placement space on each side. Six deployment candidate regions: two early, two on opposite sides of the Server, two toward the Product. Give all three play zones useful space. The mid bend feels valuable without one site covering the entire route.
Main feeling: welcoming first day on a small campus, readable balanced three-part route, restraint and clarity.

Title exactly: "02  CREEKSIDE COMPUTE"
Subtitle exactly: "A calm route beside running water"
Scene/theme: a small riverside development lab in a green park, shallow cyan creek crossing only the initial part of the route, reeds, stone banks, restrained pines at far edge, waterside cooling equipment, tiny mossy rocks. Broad lush island of land, never a dense forest. Product is a friendly riverside application lab with a broad landing plaza and code-symbol screen. Natural shoreline is the distinctive landmark.
Route topology: one open broad C-shaped shoreline curve, not a closed loop. In top-down plan ENTRY at upper-left (12%,20%), route travels right along the back at (55%,20%) over exactly ONE SHORT LOW FIXED bridge across a narrow creek, continues to (78%,30%), bends down beside a compact SERVER at (85%,48%), then sweeps left through (70%,72%) and (45%,78%) to PRODUCT lower-left (20%,78%). Server footprint near the outer middle bank, beside the path, never on it; its blind spot has placement space both upstream and downstream. Entry and Product are separated by land and do not connect. A creek/water body occupies some unused inside-left space; retain continuous useful dry land beside the curved middle and final route.
Six candidate deployment regions distributed early, both sides of the Server bend, and late. The bridge is scenery on a continuous flat route, not a gimmick, extra lane, path blocker, or height-based mechanic. No underground segments. Full route visible. Main feeling: serene natural infrastructure with a memorable creek, slightly more separated placement zones.

Title exactly: "03  LAUNCH GARDEN"
Subtitle exactly: "Grow the first release"
Scene/theme: a compact startup maker garden, warm sage and teal lawn, subtle warm apricot accents, small vegetable-like planters and wildflowers, a neat peripheral solar canopy and utility cabinet, a tiny chalk workshop at back border. Friendly modern low-poly infrastructure rather than a space launch site. Product is a distinctive small chalk launch studio with a large rounded application screen and an empty adjacent platform for future feature growth. No rockets or spaceships.
Route topology: one simple open folded U, a single broad hairpin around a central planted meadow. In top-down plan ENTRY upper-left (10%,25%). Route travels right along upper arm through (45%,25%) and (78%,25%), bends downward at the far right through (85%,50%), then travels left along lower arm through (75%,75%) and (45%,75%), ending at PRODUCT lower-left (15%,75%). Entry and Product are not connected. A compact rectangular SERVER beside the right return bend at (75%,50%) breaks sight between a central deployment area and part of the return leg. Two arms have plenty of spacing, so most tower sites can cover only one arm; one clearly limited inside-corner region can touch parts of both arms. Do not compress the two legs into a universal optimal choke.
Six proposed free-placement regions: two on the upper leg, two on opposite sides of the Server/right turn, two on the lower return leg. Central grass remains partly buildable and is not entirely consumed by decorations. All route and placement at one gameplay height. Main feeling: small team growing toward a launch, one slightly stronger placement puzzle while still introductory.
cleanup: Removed inconsistent painted arrow marks in all three views; moved Creekside's inset Server footprint entirely beside the route.
note: The diagrams and map-concepts.json are independent proposed layout data. Generated art is illustrative.
